quest.title: Wailing Cacophony
quest.description: Tlazolli has revealed her true intentions, coercing "Nechca" into her self-proclaimed "abandoned" workshop. If you wish to save the child who sought your help, you must pursue them.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x500, Mora x44000, The Cornerstone of Stars and Flames x1, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x10

chapter.num: A Prayer for Blessings, Told to Crested Peaks: Act III
chapter.title: Melodious Chant

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: You got here quick. Impressive.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nechca's up there! What are you planning to do to her!?

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: I never lied to you. All this time, I've only been trying to save my daughter.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Even though she's not my daughter yet... But once everything is over, she will really become my Nechca.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is she saying? Is she not Nechca?

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: So you've figured it out? I want to use memories to awaken my Nechca.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: She has stayed in the Night Kingdom for far too long... She's afraid of the dark and cold.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: I'm the one who made her stay there alone, so I must bring her back.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Don't worry, Nechca. Mom hasn't forgotten anything, she has always remembered your name...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I'm afraid so.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then who's that girl lying up there?

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: She's a child from my tribe. Her parents were killed in that same Abyss attack, but wouldn't you know it... Her birthday is the same as that of my Nechca.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: I raised her and took care of her for many years. I thought that taking her in would... help me feel better.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: I was so happy the first time she was willing to call me "Mom," but then... I suddenly felt very, very scared.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Is she really my child? My child's name is Nechca... It could only be Nechca.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: How could I be happy? M—My little Nechca is still waiting for me... Waiting for me to get her home.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: As I said, I only want to bring Nechca back, even if it costs me everything.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: And now, the time has come for me to pay.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: As for my useless Ancient Name... Hmph, it's finally time to put it to good use.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: If you're not willing to help me, then you can become the fuel for Nechca's Ancient Name!

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Xilonen, you have yet to make a move. I take it you're examining the Inscriptions around you?

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: It's no use. I've already set up all the Blazegem Inscriptions, and the engraving diagram has already begun to run.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: It's all thanks to your ideas. Now, the Central Inscription will finally become Nechca's Ancient Name.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: After Nechca returns, I'll make sure to invite you to her birthday party.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're... You're not gonna go up there, are you?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: There's a flaw in this engraving diagram. The weak point is almost about to activate, so on my mark...

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Don't worry, Nechca... Don't worry... Mom is here...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Three.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Mom will always be with you. I'll never forget you...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Two.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Wake up, Nechca... Now! Please, wake up...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: One!

choices.text: We can't let her harm an innocent child!

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: I saw Nechca, and was speaking with her, but now, where... Where did she go!?

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Nechca? Nechca! Where are you? Answer Mommy! Please... Please!

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Xilonen! You saw her too, didn't you? You saw my little Nechca!

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: I felt her hands and hugged her. I was right... I was right...

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Those gray shadows were just a minor mistake... I just need to restart the ritual again... Right, I'll start it again, and Nechca will...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Have you still not come to your senses, Auntie?

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Hmm? What senses? I was not wrong. Nothing about what happened was wrong!

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: She's just a little upset and was trying to ignore me... That child sure knows how to throw a tantrum... B—But I understand, I can accept that!

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Enough, Tlazolli!

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: The person you summoned with the Blazegem Inscription wasn't the real Nechca at all.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: You collected memories of Nechca from countless people, but you forgot one thing...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Among what you gathered were not only real memories but also countless emotions.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Didn't you realize what kind of emotions people would feel upon seeing Nechca's condition?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: When people held a dying child's hand... when they felt her faint breath and saw the helplessness in her eyes... When they sensed her body growing colder and colder...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: What could they feel, but abject pain and sorrow?

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: I... I took those emotions...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: You absorbed those emotions into the Blazegem Inscriptions, and solidified them as a piece of her past.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Those gray figures were projections of that past. They could only reproduce the appearance of Nechca in her sickly state.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: What the real Nechca wished to say was drowned out by those twisted and painful thoughts.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: I... I didn't want things to turn out like this... All I wanted was to remember Nechca... to see her again...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Nechca has always been with you, Auntie.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Everything has long been recorded on your Ancient Name... The one you said was "useless."

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: You exhausted every option and sacrificed everything in the hopes of saving your daughter... That's undeniable.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: But have you forgotten the true meaning of your own Ancient Name?

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: My Ancient Name is... "Und{RUBY#[D]Kinship}ugu"...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: The immovable love between you and Nechca has already been recorded in your Ancient Name, but you chose to ignore that.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: "Names are blessings from the past to the future..." You told me that, Auntie.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: You gave Nechca her name, her first blessing.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: But now, you've turned her name into a prison by taking an innocent child captive... And you've imprisoned yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Nechca is everything to me. Without her, I can't see any future for me.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: And as for blessings... Haha. What blessings have I had since the day she passed? I see her in my dreams every day, grasping my hand... telling me she's in pain, asking me to hold her.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: But I can't say anything... I can't grasp her hand... All I can do is shout her name over and over again until I wake up.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Every day... every single day, I've hated myself... and Ancient Names, too. Who knows... Maybe hate would have been the only thing left to her, too...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: You think... Nechca would have come to hate you?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Auntie, do you still remember the last words Nechca ever said to you? Do you remember what her final words really were?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: The reason you haven't felt blessed is because you've forgotten the true past... Auntie, you've been wallowing in memories of your imagination and refused to let go of them.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: A name without a past is nothing but a withered tree with no roots, rotting without a future.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: It's over, Auntie. It's all over now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, slowly now. Why don't you stay lying down? Uh, on second thought, this might not be the best place to rest...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Xilonen! Nechca... uh, Nepecha can already stand now, so we made our way over.

response.speaker: Nepecha
response.text: #Thank you, Paimon, and {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} {NICKNAME}...

response.speaker: Nepecha
response.text: I'm fine, really. The real Nechca helped me just now, so it doesn't hurt much anymore.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: That's good. If you became Nechca, then this story would really become like Tequil the Brave.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: This isn't the place to chat. Come on, let's get out of here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, but what about Tlazolli?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Don't worry, she won't be able to cause any more trouble now.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: It's all over. You leave the workshop. Once outside, Xilonen asks that you go accompany Nepecha. She still needs to have some words with Tlazolli alone...

talks.objective: Rest for a moment with Xilonen

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Alright, I've locked Auntie in the house with a few ropes. I'll take her to the tribe shortly to be punished for what she did.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: As for now, we can get away from the house and get some sun.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: After dealing with all of that, I'm completely out of energy...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She's already planned out everything... Xilonen sure doesn't waste time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sigh* It's still so scary to imagine... Tlazolli wanted to turn her adopted child into Nechca, and she even nearly succeeded...

choices.text: Good thing we found out in time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, you were so cool in the final moments, Xilonen! You went right into action and took control of the situation instantly.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: It's all thanks to Nepecha's resilience — she never gave up. If it weren't for her bravely trying to get help, then I wouldn't have noticed Auntie's plans so easily.

response.speaker: Nepecha
response.text: It was thanks to all of you encouraging me. After all, this was already the last idea I could think of...

response.speaker: Nepecha
response.text: I tried to get the attention of many others who visited before, but they were all either quickly whisked away by Tlazolli, or simply refused to believe me.

response.speaker: Nepecha
response.text: Even if I told them everything, Tlazolli would just blame my illness to cover it up.

response.speaker: Nepecha
response.text: All she had to do was start to cry, and the guests would try to comfort her, but completely forget about me.

response.speaker: Nepecha
response.text: She would inspect all the letters I sent and any gifts I received. And then... if I didn't comply, she would force me to drink some strange medicine.

response.speaker: Nepecha
response.text: It would put me to sleep for a few days, and it would be hard for me to remember anything. I would see a lot of weird things while I slept, and the walls around me would start talking.

response.speaker: Nepecha
response.text: I would be so scared every day... If I wasn't able to get your help this time, I might have just given up.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's all in the past now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #You have us now, Nepecha. If anyone dares to hurt you again, {NICKNAME} and Xilonen will send them flying!

response.speaker: Nepecha
response.text: Y—Yeah... Sorry, I... I just can't help it...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You are already super brave! And you even managed to call Xilonen for help. You definitely found the right person!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Xilonen isn't the kind of person who gets distracted easily by crying. She pays attention when someone's talking and doesn't miss a beat!

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: And it was because of your help that I was able to pick up on the details.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Without you, it would have been extremely difficult for her to communicate that she needed help.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Tlazolli would certainly be more on guard if I tried to speak with her, and would probably have just kept Nepecha locked up in her room again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So we had a part to play, too! But, where did Tlazolli even get the confidence to try this scheme? When Nechca was alive, surely many tribe members would have tried to help her.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Was she not scared that someone would realize that Nepecha wasn't Nechca?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: She must have been using the Blazegem Inscriptions for a very long time.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: That's certainly a possibility. The Inscriptions she created would not only collect information related to Nechca's past, but also actively erase people's memories of Nechca.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: It's similar to graffiti. If you want to paint something new on a wall that has been painted before, then first, you must remove the old painting.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: It's possible that I was also one of her targets, which would explain why she was so willing to let me have the Central Inscription.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, and you still took it! If it were Paimon, she would have thrown that thing away the first chance she had!

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: You can't uncover the truth without taking some risks, right? If I hadn't disassembled the Inscription myself, I would have never realized her actual motives.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you suspected her from the very beginning?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: No. She's my Auntie, after all. How could I have seen her as a villain from the start?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: The most I did was keep the possibility and a corresponding plan in mind. It was just our luck that the worst case scenario actually happened.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: But now that I look back on it, we still managed to rescue a suffering child, even if that wasn't our original intention.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Anyway, I think we've just about summarized everything and praised each other enough by now.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Everything is finally over, and Nepecha can now finally be herself.

response.speaker: Nepecha
response.text: So, what should I do now, Xilonen?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You should do whatever you like, of course! No one is going to lock you up anymore.

response.speaker: Nepecha
response.text: But, I... I don't know what I can do.

response.speaker: Nepecha
response.text: Everything I know is about Nechca... What she liked to eat, which flowers she enjoyed, how she acted and spoke.

response.speaker: Nepecha
response.text: I'm not her, but... But I can only be like her. I... I don't know, Xilonen. I just don't know...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Don't worry, Nepecha. The Blazegem Inscription isn't working anymore. No one will force you to be somebody else again.

response.speaker: Nepecha
response.text: But, I no longer remember anything about myself now besides my name. What if I never remember my life, and lose all of my past?

response.speaker: Nepecha
response.text: I'm scared, Xilonen. *sobbing* What should I do?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Don't cry, Nepecha.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Here, take this. I took some ore from Tlazolli's collection, and made this as a mold.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A Blazegem Inscription! You can make them too?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Of course not. It's just a pretty piece of stone. Take it — I've engraved your name, "Nepecha," on the top.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: This is your first blessing, the one you received from a pair of people who loved you with all of their hearts.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: It has always protected you, and stood over you. For all of past, present, and future, it's never strayed far.

response.speaker: Nepecha
response.text: ...But, I don't even remember the names of my parents. I... I don't remember anything...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I won't make any big promises and say everything will return to normal for you... I'm not sure what kind of future you will face.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I can only promise that no matter what the future holds, your name will never fade. This is a blessing given to you by a Name Engraver.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: You'll continue to grow and mature, as a sapling sprouts upward and becomes a healthy tree, or as birds spread their wings to fly high into the sky.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Your name is your starting point, as well as your guide.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Remember your name and everything you've experienced, and you'll know how to step into your future.

response.speaker: Nepecha
response.text: I... I'll do my best.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You can do it, Nepecha!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We'll always be with you.

response.speaker: Nepecha
response.text: #Thank you all... Xilonen, Paimon, and {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} {NICKNAME}...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: If you really can't come up with what to do, don't worry. Just relax and take it easy.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: We're from the same tribe, after all. If nothing else works, I can always go to the elders and look up your history.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: And until then, you can stay at my workshop. I can handle another mouth to feed.

choices.text: So you do have a backup plan...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: *sigh* I don't know if the plan will work... I'm not even sure who I should look for.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Rather than placing our hopes on a plan that relies so heavily on luck, we should just focus on ourselves.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Anyway, enough about that for now. Let me take Tlazolli back to the tribe first. Come with me, Nepecha.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Oh, gosh, I nearly forgot that we haven't even had dinner yet. What would you like to eat?

response.speaker: Nepecha
response.text: Huh? Oh, anything... I'm not picky.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Good. Let's go, we have a lot of work to do. We have a very busy future ahead of us.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Ah, and one more thing...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Happy Birthday, Nepecha.

choices.text: Do you think you can find anything about her?
Xilonen knew what to do right away.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Ah, you're here. Everything's been taken care of now. I was just about to go have a rest.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: You mean what we're doing with Auntie?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I mean, not many have ever used Ancient Names to commit a crime... Pacal will have a lot on his plate.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I do know that her workshop will be closed permanently, and any remaining incomplete Blazegem Inscriptions will be completely destroyed.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Anyway, at least her Ancient Name is fine, otherwise, we'd have a real mess on our hands...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Ah, speaking of Ancient Names, I actually have some good news. The memories that were absorbed by the Blazegem Inscriptions can be restored to their owners.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Once all the Blazegem Inscriptions stop working, the memories will return to their respective owners.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: That's right. Huh, now that I think about it... In her attempt to get Nechca to come back, Auntie made the entire tribe forget about her.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Now, Nechca really is gone, but everyone is about to remember her... What a bizarre turn of events.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: She's resting in my workshop. I contacted others from the tribe, and told them about my plan to conduct an official investigation into her history.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: The tribe hasn't responded yet, so I'm planning to take her in for now, and teach her some crafting skills.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Nepecha's learning a little slowly... But I like her attitude. Who knows? She might someday become a Name Engraver, too.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Alright, see you around. I'll let you know if anything new comes up.

dialogues.speaker: Nepecha
dialogues.text: Hi! Welcome to... to...

response.speaker: Nepecha
response.text: #Paimon and {M#Mr. {NICKNAME}}{F#Miss {NICKNAME}}! I... I'm really happy here.

response.speaker: Nepecha
response.text: Every day, there's so much for me to learn, and so much to eat... It hurts when sparks from the forge hit my hands, but I'm not scared of pain!

response.speaker: Nepecha
response.text: Xilonen even said that she's already looking into my past, though I haven't heard from her yet... but I believe in her!

response.speaker: Nepecha
response.text: Now, I write in my diary every day, recording all the interesting things that I experience.

response.speaker: Nepecha
response.text: The next time I dream of Nechca, I can tell her about it all! She'll be so happy, I know it!

response.speaker: Nepecha
response.text: I also want to tell her how I'm doing my best to study, eat, and grow up, and that she doesn't need to worry about me!

response.speaker: Nepecha
response.text: *sigh* But I haven't dreamt of her again. Could she... Did she really leave...?

response.speaker: Nepecha
response.text: #Bye, Paimon! Bye, {M#Mr. {NICKNAME}}{F#Miss {NICKNAME}}!
